title: Sunset Session

conditions.headline: Gnarly Wipeout, Then a Paddle Back to the Lineup
conditions.summary: A hot inflation read, new tariff proposals and a chip selloff knocked the S&P 500 down as much as 3.2 percent, but falling Treasury yields fueled a late comeback. The Dow and small caps finished green while the Nasdaq slipped 0.6 percent ahead of the Thanksgiving break.

sections.title: Closing Bell
items: S&P 500 closed at 7,182.78, down 18.31 points or 0.25%, after being down as much as 3.2% earlier in the day.
The Nasdaq Composite fell 147.73 points, or 0.62%, to 23,585.80 as chip stocks extended their pullback.
The Dow rose 164.25 points, or 0.33%, to 50,182.95 after erasing an intraday drop of more than 1,100 points.
The Russell 2000 gained 0.7% to 2,704.06 as small caps led and large-cap tech lagged.
Falling Treasury yields powered the afternoon recovery; energy led the sectors while technology and consumer discretionary lagged.
Even with today's dip, all four major indexes are up roughly 4% or more for the holiday-shortened week.

sections.title: Macro & Fed
items: October PCE inflation ran at 3.8% year over year, in line with forecasts; core PCE came in at 3.3%, a tenth above expectations.
Third-quarter GDP was revised up to a 4.3% annual growth rate from 3.4%.
Initial jobless claims fell to 189,000, below the 200,000 expected and near multi-decade lows.
Personal income jumped 0.7% versus 0.4% expected, while spending rose 0.3%.
Futures markets fully price a quarter-point Fed rate hike at the December 8-9 meeting.
The administration proposed new Section 301 tariffs on 14 trading partners, including 15% on the EU and Japan; chips, autos and metals are excluded and duties aren't expected before January.
The 10-year Treasury yield fell about 6 basis points to roughly 4.85%; WTI crude rose 2.5% to $84.11 and the VIX climbed 6% to near 28.

sections.title: Biggest Movers
items: HPQ (HP Inc.): +11.5% — better-than-expected quarterly results and an encouraging fiscal 2027 outlook.
LI (Li Auto): +11.0% — third-quarter revenue grew and fourth-quarter delivery guidance pleased investors.
DE (Deere): +4.4% — rebounded from a premarket dip after issuing fiscal 2027 profit guidance.
META (Meta Platforms): +3.4% — bucked the tech selloff.
NVDA (Nvidia): -3.9% — chip selloff continued and S&P Global placed its credit rating on watch, citing governance after the CEO reinstatement.
MU (Micron): -4.5% — memory and chip names extended their slide.
AMBA (Ambarella): -19.8% — guided next-quarter revenue sharply lower, citing memory prices hitting customers.
NTNX (Nutanix): -15.2% — CEO Rajiv Ramaswami will step down despite 15% revenue growth.

sections.title: Earnings Today & Tonight
items: Deere reported before the bell; it opened lower but finished up 4.4%.
Li Auto and Kanzhun reported overnight and both closed up more than 11% and 12% respectively.
Polestar fell 12.4% after its third-quarter revenue dropped 14% and it posted a $403 million loss.
Tuesday-night reporters moved today: HP surged, while Nutanix, Ambarella, GoodRx and Urban Outfitters fell sharply.
Dell, which reported a record quarter on Tuesday night, closed up 0.6%; no major companies reported after today's close.

sections.title: Business News
items: SpaceX and Tesla formed special committees to explore an all-stock merger that would value the combined company at $3.2 trillion to $3.5 trillion.
The FCC authorized SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million data-center satellites.
Nvidia's surprise reinstatement of Jensen Huang as CEO earlier this week continues to whipsaw chip stocks.
Anthropic shares closed at $82.79, just under their $83 IPO price.
Gold touched its lowest level in more than a year after the inflation data before edging higher into the close.

sections.title: On Deck
items: Thursday, November 26: US stock markets are closed for Thanksgiving.
Friday, November 27: markets reopen for a shortened session, closing early at 12:00 PM Central.
Traders will keep watching tariff headlines; public comments on the proposed tariffs are due January 5.
Next big event: the Fed's December 8-9 meeting, where a quarter-point hike is fully priced in.

script: Cowabunga! This is Surf Daddy, your local Kahuna, live from Surfside USA to all you Trade Wind surfers from the Gulf Coast to the North Shore. It's Wednesday, November twenty-fifth, twenty twenty-six, and this is your Sunset Session, the full wrap of today's market. The sun is dropping low over the water, the sky is going orange, and we are paddling in from the last set before the Thanksgiving break. Gus the wonder dog has been sniffing around the kitchen all afternoon, dreaming about turkey. Say happy Thanksgiving eve, Gus! Alright, let's talk about the final set. This was one gnarly ride. A hot inflation report, new tariff plans and another chip selloff pulled the S and P five hundred down as much as three point two percent this morning. But falling Treasury yields brought the swell back in the afternoon. The S and P five hundred closed at seven thousand one hundred eighty-three, down a quarter of a percent. The Nasdaq slipped six tenths of a percent to twenty-three thousand five hundred eighty-six. The Dow erased an eleven hundred point drop and finished up a third of a percent at fifty thousand one hundred eighty-three. Cowabunga, that is a comeback! Small caps led the way, with the Russell two thousand up seven tenths of a percent. Energy was the best sector, while tech and consumer names lagged. Now for wind and weather. October P C E inflation came in at three point eight percent from a year ago, right on forecast. But core P C E was three point three percent, a tenth hotter than expected. Third quarter growth was revised up to a strong four point three percent. Jobless claims dropped to one hundred eighty-nine thousand, better than expected. Traders now fully expect a quarter point Fed rate hike at the December meeting. The administration also proposed new tariffs on fourteen trading partners, including fifteen percent on Europe and Japan, though not before January. The ten year Treasury yield fell about six basis points to around four point eight five percent. Crude oil rose two and a half percent to eighty-four dollars, gold edged higher, bitcoin held near sixty thousand dollars, and the fear gauge, the VIX, climbed to almost twenty-eight. Let's check the lineup. HP caught the best wave of the big names, up eleven and a half percent on strong results and a bright outlook. Gus, that's worth a biscuit! Here you go, buddy! Li Auto jumped eleven percent, and Deere hung ten, flipping a morning dip into a four percent gain. Meta rose more than three percent. On the wipeout side, Nvidia fell almost four percent and Micron dropped four and a half percent. Ambarella sank about twenty percent on a weak forecast, and Nutanix fell fifteen percent after its C E O said he will step down. On the tide chart, Polestar dropped twelve percent after a big quarterly loss, while Dell edged up after its record quarter. No major companies reported after today's close. In beach talk, SpaceX and Tesla are exploring an all stock merger worth up to three and a half trillion dollars. That's a lot of sand. Anthropic shares closed just under their I P O price. Tomorrow's forecast is easy. The beach is closed for Thanksgiving. Markets reopen Friday for a short session that ends at twelve noon Central. So wax your board, enjoy the feast, and be a soul surfer this holiday. Want me to call a wave for you? Look up any stock, E T F or futures contract in the Check a Wave box on the page, and Surf Daddy will call it for you. Catch the Dawn Patrol on Friday morning. This is information, not advice. This is Surf Daddy and Gus the wonder dog saying, if in doubt, paddle out!
